name: National Theatre
watch: Ended Shell 2019; named in the May 2026 Bloomberg letter.
why_flagged: Ended Shell 2019; named in the May 2026 Bloomberg letter.
records_note: It posts annual reports with audited accounts for 2019 to 2024, names corporate, trust and individual supporters on site pages, and names its trustees.

name: National Visual Arts Gallery
funding: Owned by the Government of Malaysia and run by the National Visual Art Development Board, a statutory body under the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture. Most exhibitions are free.
watch: In February 2020 it removed four works from Ahmad Fuad Osman's retrospective. Nearly 400 artists and 55 collectors petitioned; a deputy minister sought their return.
why_flagged: Owned by the Government of Malaysia and run by the National Visual Art Development Board, a statutory body under the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture. Most exhibitions are free.
records_note: Its site names past main sponsors such as Shell and Petronas on an undated page; reports, accounts and board could not be checked.

name: Nederlands Fotomuseum
funding: Ministry of OCW and Gemeente Rotterdam give annual support. Droom en Daad funded the Santos warehouse; the Wertheimer legacy, Fonds 21, Rabobank Rotterdam Fonds and others add project money.
watch: Droom en Daad (Van der Vorm family) bought the Santos warehouse. Boijmans refused its €80M offer in 2019 after it asked for two board seats.
why_flagged: Droom en Daad (Van der Vorm family) bought the Santos warehouse. Boijmans refused its €80M offer in 2019 after it asked for two board seats.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025 with audited accounts, a named 2025 funder appendix, ANBI forms and a named supervisory board.

name: Neue Galerie New York
funding: $20.5M expenses (2023); founder Ronald Lauder (Estée Lauder cosmetics fortune) and admissions.
watch: Founder Ronald Lauder was the target of pro-Palestine protests at MoMA (2021, Nov 2024). Merging into the Met in 2028 (announced 14 May 2026).
why_flagged: Founded by Ronald Lauder, its president. Corporate members: Estée Lauder Companies, Gagosian and Orentreich Family Foundation at $25,000+; Bloomberg Philanthropies at $10,000+. It merges into the Met in 2028.
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; its Form 990-PF filings are on ProPublica, and its site names corporate members without a date.

name: Neue Nationalgalerie
funding: Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM) and Land Berlin.
watch: Nan Goldin retrospective controversy over disputed slide removal; completed in April 2025.

name: Nevada Museum of Art
watch: The 2024 donor list has San Manuel Gaming and Hospitality Authority (casino operator). Barrick is lead education sponsor; a casino-executive family is among life trustees.
why_flagged: The 2024 donor list has San Manuel Gaming and Hospitality Authority (casino operator). Barrick is lead education sponsor; a casino-executive family is among life trustees.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2012 to 2024 with a financial report, a dated donor list and sponsor list, and a named board.

name: New Holland Island
watch: Restoration and construction suspended June 2022; Fontanka links the stop to the EU freeze of Abramovich's assets in mid-March 2022; the project refused comment.
why_flagged: Restoration and construction suspended June 2022; Fontanka links the stop to the EU freeze of Abramovich's assets in mid-March 2022; the project refused comment.
records_note: The site posts no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; its project page names Millhouse and the Iris Foundation as builders and creative partners.

name: New Mexico Museum of Art
funding: State Department of Cultural Affairs unit; Museum of New Mexico Foundation revenue $16.2M (FY2025) across four museums.
watch: Vladem Contemporary: naming-rights row (2018-23) and protests over removal of Guzman's mural. FY2023 Foundation donors included Isleta Resort & Casino.
why_flagged: Vladem Contemporary: naming-rights row (2018-23) and protests over removal of Guzman's mural. FY2023 Foundation donors included Isleta Resort & Casino.
records_note: A state museum; neither it nor its Department of Cultural Affairs posts reports or accounts, but the department names the Board of Regents.

name: New Orleans Museum of Art
funding: Expenses $13.1M (2024); contributions 62%; trustees include Gayle Benson and Walda Besthoff (retail); First Horizon Bank.
watch: Flag rests on the Helis Foundation, funded by the William Helis oil family and a current sponsor of free admission. Besthoff, Zemurray and bank money is not flagged. The Taylor Energy founder's foundation is also listed in 2020.
why_flagged: Non-funding row: #DismantleNOMA racism claims (2020) and the June 2023 backlash over a curator hire. The current donor roster is unpublished (last one is 2019).
records_note: NOMA posts annual reports for 2011 to 2020, financial statements for 2011 to 2021, a donor list inside the 2020 report and its 2026 trustees.

name: New York Academy of Art
watch: Epstein sat on the Academy's board from 1987 to 1994 and met student Maria Farmer there in 1995; Farmer reported him to the FBI in 1996, the first report against him. After his 2008 conviction he bought a $25,000 table at the Academy's Tribeca Ball in 2012 and in 2014, gave $30,000 for scholarship support in 2014, and attended Academy events.
why_flagged: Van Cleef & Arpels sponsors its Tribeca Ball for scholarships. Epstein, a board member 1987 to 1994, paid $65,900 for events in 2012 and 2014, the Academy says.
records_note: Its site names 29 trustees but posts no annual report, financial statements or donor list; Form 990s and a 2025 audit are on ProPublica.

name: Nicosia Municipal Arts Centre (NiMAC)
funding: Nicosia Municipality and the Pierides Foundation run it under a cooperation agreement. Shows credit the Deputy Ministry of Culture, A.G. Leventis Foundation and European University Cyprus. No budget is published.
watch: A 2026 show with Emin Cizenel, who designed the north's flag, drew a small protest and a deputy mayor's call to cancel. No cancellation reported.
why_flagged: Nicosia Municipality and the Pierides Foundation run it under a cooperation agreement. Shows credit the Deputy Ministry of Culture, A.G. Leventis Foundation and European University Cyprus. No budget is published.
records_note: One annual report covers 2024 and 2025; no accounts, funder list or board appear, though exhibition pages credit funders.

name: Noguchi Museum
records_note: Names its trustees and posts dated benefit donor listings; direct reads were blocked, so only ProPublica filings for 2003 to 2025 were opened.
